It reads out the words the page gives it instead." --- A picture is a file of its own. The page does not hold the picture: it says which file to show, and what the picture is for people who cannot see it. ## Predict ```step stage: predict code: page.html#misspelt insight: "Most students expect the close name to work, or an error; seeing the alt words appear shows what alt is for." check: type: predict q: "The picture file is called trophy.svg, but the code says trophey.svg. What will the page show?" options: - "The trophy anyway: the name is close enough" - "An error message" - "The words A gold trophy, with a small broken-picture icon" - "Nothing at all where the picture should be" fault: runtime misconception: img-file-name actual: "The words A gold trophy (with a broken-picture icon). The browser cannot find a file with that exact name, so it shows the alt words instead." ``` `` shows a picture. `src` names the picture file, and `alt` describes it. What do you think the page will show? ## Run ```step stage: run code: page.html#misspelt try: { playground: html, starter: "page.html#misspelt", height: 380 } insight: "src must match the file name exactly; alt is what people get when they cannot see the picture." check: { type: reflect, text: "I can explain what alt is for." } unlocks: [img-image] ``` Compare the page with your prediction. The alt words show because the browser cannot find a file called `trophey.svg`. The table says what each part does. | Code | What it does | Why | |---|---|---| | `` | Shows a picture | `` has no closing tag: there are no words to wrap, so everything it needs is in its attributes | | `src="trophy.svg"` | Names the picture file | The picture is a separate file. The name, the ending after the dot and the capitals must match the file exactly, or the browser cannot find it | | `alt="A gold trophy"` | Says what the picture shows | Screen readers read it aloud, and the browser shows it when the picture cannot load. It is not a caption: people who can see the picture do not see it | | `width="100"` | Sets the picture's width in pixels | Another attribute. Without it the picture shows at its own size | ## Investigate ```step stage: investigate code: page.html#parts insight: "alt is for people who cannot see the picture, not a caption; src has to match the file exactly." tasks: - check: type: question q: "When does a person who can see the picture also see its alt words?" options: - "Under the picture, as its caption" - "Only when the picture does not load, or when a screen reader reads the page aloud" - "When they hold the mouse over the picture" - "At the top of the page, as a title" answer: 1 fault: logic misconception: alt-is-caption explain: "alt is not shown beside a picture that loads. It stands in for the picture when it cannot be seen. A caption is a separate line of text, written as a paragraph." - check: type: question q: "Which alt is best for a photo of the relay team holding the trophy?" options: - "alt=\"image\"" - "alt=\"relay-photo.jpg\"" - "alt=\"The Owls relay team holding the trophy\"" - "No alt at all" answer: 2 fault: logic misconception: alt-is-caption explain: "alt should say what the picture shows, as you would describe it to someone on the phone. A word such as image, or the file name, tells them nothing." - check: type: bug code: page.html#wrongfile answer: 4 fault: runtime misconception: img-file-name text: "The trophy shows, but the medal does not: only its alt words appear. The picture file is called medal.svg. Click the line that causes it." explain: "Line 4 asks for medal.png, but the file is medal.svg. The name, the ending after the dot and the capitals must all match the file exactly." ``` ### Where does alt show? Think about who needs the words. ### Good alt text Imagine describing the picture to someone on the phone. ### The missing medal One picture does not show. ## Modify ```step stage: modify insight: "src picks the file, alt describes it, width sizes it: each is its own attribute, changed on its own." try: { playground: html, starter: "page.html#modify", height: 420 } tasks: - hint: - "The file name is the part inside the quotes after `src=`." - "The picture to show is `medal.svg`. Match the name exactly." check: { type: code, text: "Show the medal picture instead of the trophy.", rules: { contains: ["src=\"medal.svg\""] } } expected: page.html#sol-src - hint: - "`alt` is the attribute with the words in quotes." - "Describe the medal as you would to someone on the phone: A silver medal." check: { type: code, text: "Change the alt words to A silver medal.", rules: { contains: ["alt=\"A silver medal\""] } } expected: page.html#sol-alt - hint: "Change the number inside the quotes after `width=`." check: { type: code, text: "Make the picture 200 wide.", rules: { contains: ["width=\"200\""] } } expected: page.html#sol-width ``` ### Change the picture Show `medal.svg` instead of the trophy. Only the file name changes. ### Change the alt words The alt words still describe a trophy. Change them to `A silver medal`. ### Change the size Make the picture `200` wide. ## Mix it up ```step stage: investigate insight: "A picture inside a link combines the image tag with an attribute on the tag around it." check: type: parsons code: page.html#review extra: [""] text: "Put the lines in order so that clicking the trophy picture opens the results. One line is not needed." explain: "The link's opening tag, with its href, comes first; the picture goes inside it; closes the link. An has no closing tag, so is not needed." ``` Make the picture itself the thing people click. ## Make ```step stage: make try: { playground: html, starter: "page.html#make", height: 420 } hint: - "Pick one picture. Its file name goes in `src`." - "Write `alt` as if describing the picture to someone on the phone." check: type: code text: "Make a page with a title, a picture with alt, and a paragraph." rules: { tags: [h1, img, p], contains: ["alt=\""] } expected: page.html#sol-make smaller: check: type: question q: "Which tag shows the trophy picture and describes it for someone who can't see it?" options: - "" - "" - "" - "" answer: 0 feedback: - null - "A picture's file goes in src, not href, and it needs alt text too." - "The tag is img, short for image." - "The file name goes in src. The alt is for the words that describe it." explain: "img needs two attributes: src, which file to show, and alt, what to say about it." ``` Make a page about a sport, a book or a band you like: a title, a picture, and a paragraph about it. The pictures you can use are `trophy.svg`, `medal.svg`, `book.svg`, `ball.svg`, `star.svg` and `music.svg`. ```teacher summary: Students show a picture with img, and learn that src must match the file name exactly and that alt describes the picture for people who cannot see it. time: 40 timing: "Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 8 min · Modify 8 min · Mix it up 4 min · Make 10 min" goals: - I can show a picture with . - I can say why the file name in src must match exactly. - I can write alt words that describe what the picture shows. before: | Read the unit primer "Lists, links and pictures in 5 minutes" first, then do the Make task yourself in the playground (about 5 minutes). An `` tag has no closing tag, and the picture is a separate file. `src` names the file and `alt` describes it. The pictures students can use without uploading are `trophy.svg`, `medal.svg`, `book.svg`, `ball.svg`, `star.svg` and `music.svg`. Two ideas to land: a file name that is nearly right still fails, and alt is not a caption. running: - "Predict and Run: many students pick the first option, that the close name still works. Let them run it and see the alt words. Fixing the name comes in Modify." - "Investigate: the first question is the one for alt-is-caption. Ask who actually reads alt. Then they apply it to the relay photo and the missing medal." - "Modify: three single changes: the file, the alt words, then the size. Misspell the name once on purpose and ask what shows." - "Mix it up: the picture inside a link needs the attribute lesson. Ask where the href goes." - "Make: the check ticks when the page has a heading, a picture with alt and a paragraph; read their alt words as a class." stuck: - see: The picture shows as words and a small broken icon. ask: Is the file name in src spelt exactly like the file, with the same ending? fix: Copy the file name from the list of pictures, including .svg. - see: The student typed alt words but sees none under the picture. ask: When do people see alt? fix: alt only shows when the picture cannot load, and screen readers read it. A caption would be a paragraph under the picture. - see: Words after the picture are inside the tag, or the picture vanishes. ask: Does the img tag end with > and have no closing tag? fix: End the tag with > straight after the last attribute and start the next element after it. stretch: "Add a second picture with its own alt, and make one of the pictures a link to a page." support: "Give students the Modify starter and do the first task together, then change the alt words and the width." leads: "Next lesson names some of the elements with a class so that a CSS rule can style only those. Class idea: ask what a person using a screen reader hears when the alt says image." exit: q: "A student's picture does not show, only a few words. What do they check first, and what are the words?" a: "They check that the file name in src matches the file exactly. The words are the alt text, which shows when the picture cannot load." explain: | The video and the picture show the same steps: 1. `` shows a picture and has no closing tag. 2. `src` names the picture file, and the name must match exactly. 3. `alt` says what the picture shows. With a wrong `src`, people see the alt words instead. solutions: step-4#t1: page.html#sol-src step-4#t2: page.html#sol-alt step-4#t3: page.html#sol-width step-6: page.html#sol-make struggle: "Believing that a nearly right file name will do. Let them see the alt words, then ask what the browser can compare the name to." class: activities: - at: predict kind: discussion title: Close enough? minutes: 3 do: | With your partner, decide what the page shows when one letter of the file name is wrong. Hold up 1, 2, 3 or 4 fingers for your answer. notes: "Take a vote before running. Ask what the browser has to compare the name with. The aim is that the name must be exactly the file's." - at: end kind: activity title: Describe it to me minutes: 4 do: | Read your alt words to a partner without showing the picture. They say which picture you used. notes: "A good alt lets the partner pick the right picture. If they cannot, ask what is missing from the words." ``` ```code page.html#misspelt
